```{r}
library(torch)
library(torchvision)
library(ggplot2)

df <- read.csv("data.csv")
head(df)
```


```{r}
# write a function that will display the image
plot_img <- function(x, im_shape = c(6, 6)) {
  # need to convert matrix to data frame for ggplot
  df <- data.frame(expand.grid(x = 1:im_shape[2], y = 1:im_shape[1]),
                   value = as.vector(t(x)))
  
  ggplot(df, aes(x, y, fill = value)) +
    geom_tile() +
    # can choose how to map the 0 and 1 (I'm copying cmap from python here)
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "black", high = "white") +
    theme_void() +
    theme(aspect.ratio = 1) +
    scale_y_reverse()
}
```


```{r}
X <- df[,!names(df) %in% c("language")]
y <- df$language


# Split the data
set.seed(42)
# An easy way to get some indices
# about 75% training data
train_indices <- sample(1:nrow(X), size = round(nrow(X)*.75), replace = F) 

# split
X_train <- as.matrix(X[train_indices, ])
X_test <- as.matrix(X[-train_indices, ])
y_train <- y[train_indices]
y_test <- y[-train_indices]

x_train <- X_train / 255
x_test <- X_test / 255

x_train <- torch_tensor(array(x_train, dim = c(dim(x_train)[1], 1, 128, 128)), dtype = torch_float())
x_test <- torch_tensor(array(x_test, dim = c(dim(x_test)[1], 1, 128, 128)), dtype = torch_float())

x_test
```



```{r}
# images need to be transposed as all are sideways
plot_img(t(as.matrix(x_test[nrow(x_test),1,,])), im_shape = c(128, 128))
```

```{r}
cnn_model <- nn_module(
  initialize = function() {
    # the channels are both 1 because we have black and white images (single matrix for each image)
    # this is the convolutional layer
    # this implementation is much slower than keras, so I'm going to use a bigger kernel (7 by 7)
    self$conv <- nn_conv2d(in_channels = 1, out_channels = 1, kernel_size = 3, stride = 1)
    # pooling layer
    self$pool <- nn_max_pool2d(kernel_size = 2)
    # this is the hidden layer (I'm also speeding up things by making the network less wide)
    self$hid <- nn_linear(in_features = 126 * 126, out_features = 15000) 
    
    # self$hid2 <- nn_linear(in_features = 250, out_features = 100)
    # this is the output layer
    self$out <- nn_linear(in_features = 15000, out_features = 1)
  },
  # we're just going to call the data x which will be passed through each layer:
  forward = function(x) {
    x <- self$conv(x)
    x <- torch_flatten(x, start_dim = 2) # Flatten except for channel dimension
    x <- self$hid(x)
    x <- torch_relu(x)
    #x <- self$hid2(x)
    #x <- torch_tanh(x)
    x <- self$out(x)
    torch_sigmoid(x)
  }
)
```
